summary.intent: Coordinate subagents that fix two monokl search behaviors: searching non-UTF-8 files lossily instead of dropping them, and applying parent .gitignore/.ignore files (bounded at the repo root) when searching a subdirectory.
summary.outcome: Two PRs were opened and left unmerged with CI pending: #57 (lossy non-UTF-8 reads with a new LossyRead diagnostic) and #58 (parent ignore files applied up to the repo root). Both passed local lint and tests, but neither ran the full `just ci`. Merge ordering with #55 and #56 is still to be settled.

repo: Diagnostic has no payload variants, so structured info is carried by a DiagnosticKind variant (e.g. LossyRead, serialized as "lossyread") with a fixed message string.
diagnostic_lines in output/agent.rs groups diagnostics by kind and prints up to 3 paths plus '...and N more'. New kinds reuse this.
The project uses `just lint`, `just test` (nextest), `just changesets` and `just ci` (coverage, MSRV, audit). Each PR needs a changeset file under .changeset/.
text_search.rs holds the only WalkBuilder; the pipeline's second search call goes through the same function.
The `ignore` crate's parents(true) reads all ancestors up to / and cannot be bounded at the repo root, so parent ignore rules must be applied manually in filter_entry with parents(false).
Utf8Path cannot hold non-UTF-8 paths. They are counted separately in non_utf8_paths and unchanged by these PRs.
Design decisions are recorded in docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md (§18 binary/unreadable files; the 'Ignore scope' entry).

code.finding: Removed the not_utf8 flag so a non-UTF-8 matching line is a hit with U+FFFD replacement, and added manual parent .ignore/.gitignore handling in filter_entry from the repo root down to the search root's parent.

read_source now reads bytes and decodes lossily, returning Source { text, lossy }. The pipeline emits one LossyRead diagnostic per lossy file. Required-term matching runs on the lossily decoded text, so a pattern spanning an invalid byte could fail.
Added DiagnosticKind::LossyRead, pinned by tests_types.rs. #55 deletes tests_types.rs, so #57 will conflict with it.

workflow: Verify a regression test by running it against main's source and confirming it fails before the fix. The agent did this for the CLI test (it failed with search[1]).
Disabling the new behavior and counting failing tests (8 of 127) is a way to check that the tests exercise the change.
Comparing against real `rg --files` output and pinning it in a test validates ignore semantics against a reference implementation.
Subagent reports are model output; the main session relays them as unverified and flags what was not run.

friction: The first `git checkout -b` hit a config-lock error in the sandbox, though the branch was still created.
Cargo and git needed the sandbox disabled.
The nextest run reported '1 leaky' on one run of the #58 work, and the agent did not check whether its changes caused it.
#57 will conflict with #55 (tests_types.rs deleted), and #58 will likely conflict with #57 in text_search.rs and the docs.
open_items: Merge #55 first, then #56, then rebase #57 onto main. Rebase whichever of #57 and #58 merges second.
User decision: whether global git excludes and .git/info/exclude should be honored to match ripgrep. They are currently kept off deliberately.
Known gap: a parent .gitignore still applies below a nested repo inside the search root, whereas git and ripgrep stop at the nested .git.
Only .git is treated as a repo marker. The ignore crate also recognizes .jj, which was not added.
A non-UTF-8 line matching an excluded term now drops the file with no diagnostic, and a non-UTF-8 file with no analyzer gets no lossy diagnostic.
Required-term matching after lossy decoding can miss patterns that span an invalid byte (noted in the #57 PR).
CI for #57 and #58 is pending and the full `just ci` was not run for either.
Investigate the '1 leaky' nextest warning seen during #58 work.
Parent ignore files in `unreadable` are named by canonical path rather than the path the user typed.
